articles.body: Admin → Articles and menus → Staff discounts Create a named discount Create a name and choose fixed amount, fixed percentage, variable amount or variable percentage. Enter a value for fixed definitions and save the active state. Apply with permission Select an active staff discount on the POS and enter the value when variable. Review eligible check/item scope and final balance before confirming. Distinguish online codes This staff library is separate from guest promotional codes. Do not assume that a staff discount is redeemable online or available to every employee.

articles.title: Variants & Sizes
articles.description: Set up size or flavor variants on a menu item, with per-variant price, portion, and stock status.
articles.body: Open the corresponding Foody workspace described below. What Variants Are A variant is a version of the same item sold at a distinct price. Common cases: Sizes: Small / Medium / Large. Styles: Classic / Spicy. Bowls: 250 ml / 500 ml. Meat choices: Chicken / Beef. Variants live on the item. When a customer orders, they pick exactly one per variant group. One item can have multiple variant groups (e.g. "Size" + "Sauce"), but this is rarely needed. For customer-selectable extras, use Modifiers instead. --- Creating a Variant Group 1. Open the item in Menu → Items . 2. In the Détails tab, scroll to the Variantes section. 3. Click Ajouter (or Modifier if one already exists). 4. Give the group a name (e.g. "Taille", "Size", "Flavor"). This is internal-ish — customers see the rows, not the group name. 5. Add one row per variant. Each row has: Name — shown to the customer ("Normal", "Grand", "250 g"). Price — replaces the item's base price when this variant is selected. Portion — size of the serving (with unit: g, ml, kg, l, unit). Status — Available / Out of stock. 6. Click Terminé . --- Understanding Each Field Understanding Each Field Name The label the customer picks. Keep it short and natural ("Normal", "Grand", "Petit", "XL"). Price Absolute price — not a delta. Typing 70 for Normal and 140 for Grand makes the item cost exactly that per variant, regardless of the item's base price. Portion Two related jobs: 1. What customers see on the web menu: "Grand 500 g" under the variant label. 2. Recipe scaling on the Recette tab: ingredients scoped as "Match item size" use the variant's portion as the consumed quantity. See Ingredients & Portions. Pick a unit family consistent with your recipe: Soup: ml. Hamburger: unit. Plate: g. Status Toggle to Out of stock when you're sold out for the day. The variant grays out on POS / web without deleting it. Flip back to Available when restocked. --- Reusing a Variant Group Across Items Variant groups in Foody are backed by Option Sets — a reusable pool. When you type a name that matches an existing Option Set, you get a suggestion to apply it. Applying an existing group attaches its rows to this item. You can then override per-item: Price (different price for this item). Portion. Status. Updating the name of a row on the Option Set level propagates everywhere. Useful for "Size" groups shared across many burgers. --- Removing or Hiding a Variant Hide temporarily (keeping history intact): flip Status → Out of stock. Recommended for seasonal or sold-out items. Delete : trash icon on the row. Deletes the variant from this item; if it's on an Option Set used elsewhere, it stays there. Deleting a variant that has order history doesn't touch the past orders — they still show the variant name and price as sold. --- Examples Examples Burger sizes Variant Price Portion --- --- --- Normal ₪70 1 unit Grand ₪140 2 unit On the Recette tab, flag the beef ingredient as "Custom per variant" with 200 g for Normal, 400 g for Grand. Bread / sauce stay Fixed. Soup bowls Variant Price Portion --- --- --- Bowl ₪18 250 ml Large bowl ₪32 500 ml On the Recette tab, the soup prep ingredient is scoped as "Match item size". No quantity to type; the system draws 250 ml or 500 ml automatically. Drink sizes Variant Price Portion --- --- --- Small ₪12 330 ml Medium ₪16 500 ml Large ₪22 750 ml --- What Next How to Configure Ingredients & Portions — hook variants into your recipe and cost. Creating a Menu Item — full item walkthrough.

articles.title: Restaurant calendar and exceptions
articles.description: Admin → Restaurant calendar
articles.body: Admin → Restaurant calendar Inspect a date Select the calendar period and the relevant service/date. Review the scheduled entries and restaurant timezone before making an exception. Add or edit an exception Use the date’s offered exception controls, set the affected service/hours and save. Review the calendar result and the corresponding guest availability. Remove an obsolete exception Review the affected date before removing an exception. Confirm that normal scheduling now applies; existing orders still need individual review if their fulfillment changed.

articles.title: Seats, courses, hold and fire
articles.description: Open the active table bill. Course availability depends on the restaurant’s POS profile and deployed API capabilities.
articles.body: Open the active table bill. Course availability depends on the restaurant’s POS profile and deployed API capabilities. Availability and access Advanced actions appear only when the installed POS and API advertise the required capability and your role permits them. Refresh a changed bill before retrying; never create another charge to resolve an uncertain result. Assign seats and courses Before sending, assign items to Table or selected guests and choose their course. Check course order and required item options. Financial seat allocation can later change without rewriting already-sent kitchen seating. Hold or fire a course Review the held course and use Fire to release the selected eligible food. Shared physical units launch once even when their price is split. Refresh after uncertainty rather than sending the same food as a new sale. A historical shared batch can block a partial release. Repeat food as a new sale Where Repeat is offered, review the copied food in the provisional cart and send through normal validation. The action does not copy a fractional charge or previous offering into a new payment. Stock changes only through the normal new-order flow.

articles.title: Discount, comp and void
articles.description: Select the item or bill and open its available Actions/Options. Check whether it is a draft, sent food or a saved financial share.
articles.body: Select the item or bill and open its available Actions/Options. Check whether it is a draft, sent food or a saved financial share. Availability and access Advanced actions appear only when the installed POS and API advertise the required capability and your role permits them. Refresh a changed bill before retrying; never create another charge to resolve an uncertain result. Apply a reduction Choose an allowed library or manual amount/percentage discount, its scope and any required reason. Review the resulting total before saving. An item reduction and a whole-cart reduction have different bases; online promotion codes are separate. Offer or undo an offering Choose Comp/Offer and the required reason. Offering changes the amount charged, not the food already prepared. For saved split items it affects only the selected eligible share. Removing the offering requires permission and restores its recorded amount. Cancel food with a reason Use Void only for eligible unpaid food and supply its reason. Prepared/completed food or a paid/claimed fraction can prevent cancellation. For sent food, verify the cancellation result and kitchen ticket rather than deleting a draft line. Void is not a payment refund.

articles.title: Managing Orders
articles.description: Every order from web, QR and POS in one live list. Track status, accept, send to the kitchen, and follow an order through to completion.
articles.body: Open the corresponding Foody workspace described below. What Is It? The Orders screen is one live list of every order — whether it came from the guest web app, a QR table, or the POS. From here you track status, accept orders, and send them to the kitchen. How It Works (Simply) - New orders appear in real time (a Live badge shows the connection is active). - Use the status tabs to filter — new, in kitchen, ready, completed. - Open an order to see its items, customer, and totals, and to move it along. Order flow 1. Placed — a paid web/QR order, or a POS order, arrives. 2. Accepted — you accept it (or it auto-accepts, depending on your workflow settings). 3. In kitchen — sent to preparation; a kitchen ticket can print automatically. 4. Ready / Completed — handed to the customer. Tip: workflow behavior (auto-accept, auto-send-to-kitchen, auto-print) is configured in Settings . See Workflow settings. Good to know - Orders only appear once paid (for prepaid channels), so the kitchen never sees an unconfirmed order. - If a dish sold out while the customer was ordering, checkout blocks it — see Availability.

articles.title: Move, merge and transfer items
articles.description: Open the table bill or a saved item’s Options. Whole-bill movement and selected-item transfer are different actions.
articles.body: Open the table bill or a saved item’s Options. Whole-bill movement and selected-item transfer are different actions. Availability and access Advanced actions appear only when the installed POS and API advertise the required capability and your role permits them. Refresh a changed bill before retrying; never create another charge to resolve an uncertain result. Move a bill Choose Move, select an authorized destination and read the confirmation before saving. Reopen the destination to verify the bill and covers. Moving a financial bill does not resend food to the kitchen. A payment in progress can block movement. Merge occupied table bills Choose the supported merge action and an authorized unpaid target, then review both totals/covers. The visible merged bill retains the original pricing policies and food history. Review its new balance before taking a single payment. Paid or actively claimed bills cannot be merged. Transfer saved items Open the saved item → Options → Move, choose an existing authorized table bill and confirm. A regular quantity line moves its quoted units; isolate one portion with Split first if needed. Covers stay with their bills; moved items begin at Table at the destination. Unsent drafts and named non-table tickets are outside this saved-table path. Kitchen history and stock are not duplicated.

articles.title: Review and edit an order
articles.description: Admin → Orders → select an order
articles.body: Admin → Orders → select an order Availability and access Order changes require orders.manage; read access alone does not permit edits. Find the right order Choose order/date basis, status and fulfillment filters. Open the order and verify number, customer, service date and payment status before acting. Create a staff order Use New order, select items/options and fill the required contact and fulfillment fields. Review the total and submit once; check the created order before retrying an uncertain result. Edit saved details Use the available edit action to change customer, address or fulfillment details. Save and reread the order; review preparation, fees and date restrictions before changing an existing schedule. Accept, prepare and hand over Use only the next status actions offered for the order. Verify acceptance, kitchen, ready and handover results separately from payment. Check consequences before rejection or cancellation. Send customer messages deliberately Open customer messages to inspect attempts and delivery evidence. Preview a recap/reminder before sending; an uncertain send must be checked, not repeated automatically.

articles.title: Order types and fulfillment
articles.description: Foody supports dine-in, pickup, delivery, and scheduled orders. Learn what each means and how to enable them.
articles.body: Admin → Settings → Orders / POS → order entry Dine-in and tables Select dine-in and the intended table/session when offered. Check seats and guest count separately; order type does not assign a physical table by itself. Pickup Enable pickup in the restaurant settings, then check the offered date/time and preparation delay. The customer collects at the configured location. Delivery Require a usable delivery address and check zone, fee and fulfillment window. A delivery day can be saved before its final time window is confirmed. Scheduled and batch orders Review ordering windows, cutoff and fulfillment dates. With a batch calendar, use the restaurant-defined cycle instead of inventing a free date.

articles.title: Preorders, slots and batch cycles
articles.description: Admin → Settings → Order taking → Preorders
articles.body: Admin → Settings → Order taking → Preorders Choose the intake policy Select whether preordering is disabled, offered alongside other orders, or required using the offered policy controls. Check enabled pickup/delivery services separately. Configure date/time slots Choose the slot calendar and set offered lead time, horizon and fulfillment windows. Test boundary dates in the preview rather than assuming all calendar dates are available. Configure a batch cycle Set ordering opening, cutoff and fulfillment days/windows for the cycle. Review pickup and delivery windows separately and inspect the generated cycle preview. Check payment and product exceptions Review the prepayment policy and product-specific exceptions. Save, reopen settings and test the published guest path without making a live payment as a test.

articles.title: Production quantities and packing
articles.description: Admin → Orders → Production / POS → Scheduled calendar
articles.body: Admin → Orders → Production / POS → Scheduled calendar Select the service date Select the intended service/date and inspect included orders. Compare quantities with the same date basis used by Orders and the dashboard. Review item and portion quantities Review aggregated items, variants, portions and notes before assigning preparation. Recheck the plan after a saved order change. Prepare customer packing Use the customer/order breakdown to organize packing and pickup/delivery handover. Confirm completed preparation with the offered controls; preparation does not confirm payment.

articles.title: Split and recombine bills
articles.description: Open the saved table bill → Actions → Split. Choose by cover, item or equal parts where available.
articles.body: Open the saved table bill → Actions → Split. Choose by cover, item or equal parts where available. Availability and access Advanced actions appear only when the installed POS and API advertise the required capability and your role permits them. Refresh a changed bill before retrying; never create another charge to resolve an uncertain result. Allocate covers or items By cover creates bills for assigned guests with items and shares multi-guest items. Table items and unused covers remain on the original. By item lets you select and assign items; equal parts divides the selected amount. The displayed plan remains provisional until Save. Share selected items Select complete items then Share item(s). Choose equal or custom parts and enter the count or amounts. Complete the exact selected total; review each bill, reductions, fees and covers before Save. Custom item amounts allocate food value and do not collect a payment. Recombine saved fractions Return every unpaid part of the same original unit to its original bill/ledger anchor, then use Regroup when offered. Paid, missing, actively claimed or mixed offered/charged parts cannot be regrouped. Regroup before subdividing a saved fraction again. Back/Discard leaves the saved plan unchanged.

articles.title: Take an order on the POS
articles.description: How to open a table or start a counter order, add items with modifiers, and send to the kitchen.
articles.body: POS → Tables / Order entry Start the intended check Choose the table or counter order and verify the active check, service and employee. Existing separated checks retain their own balances. Add and customize items Choose a visible POS menu group, item, active variant and allowed modifiers. Review quantity, notes and price before adding. Required choices must be completed. Assign seats and courses Where enabled, assign the item to a seat, shared table or course before sending. These preparation assignments are distinct from later financial bill splitting. Send and verify preparation Review pending items and use the configured kitchen-send action. Check the saved order and kitchen result; printer success and order persistence are separate outcomes. Resume or collect payment Reopen the saved check to add items or start payment. Confirm the selected check and unpaid balance before charging; do not resend already-sent food.

articles.title: Understanding payment status
articles.description: Check confirmed payments and handle uncertain results safely.
articles.body: Open the corresponding Foody workspace described below. Payment configuration The payment provider is configured for each restaurant by the Foody team through the backoffice. Available payment methods depend on that configuration, the merchant contract and the order channel. Sumit and Verifone are integrated; availability must be confirmed for your installation. New PayPlus checkout is disabled. Check an online payment 1. Open the order in Orders . 2. Check its payment status and recorded method. 3. A return from a payment page is not by itself proof of payment. Foody verifies the payment with the provider before marking it paid. 4. For online orders requiring payment, confirmation makes the order available to the POS workflow. A failed or uncertain result Do not assume that a timeout means no money was taken. Check the order and provider transaction before retrying a charge. Contact Foody support if they disagree or the outcome is unclear. Never include full card details, CVV or credentials in a support message. Cash/manual recording, receipts, invoice issuance and refunds are separate operations. Their available controls depend on your setup and permissions. Do not record a card payment as successful solely because a customer shows a return page. Ask support for the procedure applicable to your provider before a refund or correction.

articles.title: Take payments on the POS
articles.description: Open the intended bill and verify its current amount before Pay. Available tenders depend on the restaurant and device configuration.
articles.body: Open the intended bill and verify its current amount before Pay. Available tenders depend on the restaurant and device configuration. Record cash Choose cash, enter the received amount when requested and review change before confirming. Record only money actually received. On split bills select the correct financial bill so its receipt and paid status remain independent. Collect a connected payment Choose an enabled connected tender and follow the terminal or hosted page. Wait for Foody’s verified final status; browser return alone is insufficient. If the result is pending/uncertain, refresh and review the provider transaction with an authorized operator before any retry. Never ask the help assistant to inspect card details. Review tips and receipt Review any supported tip/checkout prompt before collection and confirm the total. After success open the digital or configured printer receipt. A reprint does not collect another payment. Per-bill refund controls are not established for every advanced split flow; contact an authorized operator rather than assuming a refund button exists.

articles.title: Payment providers, saved methods and Cibus
articles.description: Open Settings → Payments or Cibus with the required permission. Provider availability is specific to the restaurant’s contract and deployed integration.
articles.body: Open Settings → Payments or Cibus with the required permission. Provider availability is specific to the restaurant’s contract and deployed integration. Arrange provider activation Payment-provider credentials and activation are managed by the Foody team in the protected backoffice. Contact an authorized Foody operator to change them; the merchant Payments page does not connect a card processor. Use sandbox development to verify the supported transaction path. Never send credentials or card data to chat. SUMIT/Verifone availability depends on the contract; a provider name alone does not prove activation. Understand saved payment methods For an eligible customer/provider, saving a method requires its explicit enrollment flow. Guest checkout remains possible without enrollment where offered. Removing Foody’s saved authorization does not remove unrelated provider subscriptions. A failed enrollment can be reported after a successful order payment without undoing that payment. Configure and use Cibus In Cibus check whether the integration is enabled. With settings permission, replace the complete restaurant ID, POS ID and company code through the protected form; masked hints are not replacement credentials. Review the saved masked status. On POS select Cibus only when configured and inspect its result and remaining balance before another tender. A failed network response does not prove there was no charge. Set payment policy, VAT and tips In Settings → Payments review online-payment-only policy, default VAT and tips enablement. Only permitted, changed fields are saved. An unknown policy remains unknown until explicitly chosen; editing VAT must not silently choose it. Weight authorization buffer and fixed suggested-tip/rounding behavior are read-only or have no edit contract here. Verify saved values after success; retain edits on a failed save.

articles.title: Set up an Epson TM-U220IIB with Foody
articles.description: From unboxing to the first kitchen ticket: network setup, Epson Server Direct Print, FoodyAdmin registration, stations, routing, and testing.
articles.body: Open the corresponding Foody workspace described below. What you need - The printer and its Epson power supply. - A compatible ribbon cassette and 76 mm paper roll. - An Ethernet cable connected to the restaurant router or switch. - A computer or iPad on the same network during setup. - A FoodyAdmin owner or manager account with printer-management permission. - A router DHCP reservation, recommended so WebConfig remains easy to reach. Do not use a guest network. Guest Wi-Fi commonly isolates devices. Foody does not require an incoming port at the restaurant: the printer makes an outbound HTTPS connection to Foody. 1. Unbox and inspect the printer 1. Remove the printer, power supply, power cord, and ribbon cassette from the box. 2. Remove all transport foam, tape, and protective material. 3. Check the label underneath or behind the printer. Record the exact model, serial number, and MAC address. 4. Place the printer away from splashes, steam, and heat, leaving room to open both covers. 5. Keep the printer switched off while connecting cables. The MAC address identifies the network interface and can be used for a DHCP reservation. 2. Load the ribbon and paper 2. Load the ribbon and paper Ribbon cassette 1. With the printer off, open the ribbon cover. 2. Take up slack by gently turning the cassette knob in the indicated direction. 3. Fit the cassette flat and press until it is seated. 4. Close the cover without forcing it. The print head may be very hot after use. Do not touch it or force the ribbon carriage by hand. Paper roll 1. Open the paper cover with its release lever. 2. Insert the roll in the direction shown inside the cover. Paper should unwind without tension. 3. Pull a few centimetres of paper straight out. 4. Close the cover fully and tear off the excess at the tear bar. 3. Connect the printer to the network 1. Connect Ethernet between the printer and the router or switch. 2. Connect the Epson power supply to the printer, then to a reliable outlet. 3. Power on and wait for the error light to go out. 4. Print a network status sheet with the status button on the Ethernet interface. Its position depends on the installed interface; do not use the reset button. 5. Find the IPv4 address , for example 192.168.1.48 . If the address is 0.0.0.0 or missing, check the cable and switch port. An address beginning with 169.254 means the router did not provide an address. 4. Open Epson TMNet WebConfig 1. From the computer or iPad on the same network, open https://IP-ADDRESS . If HTTPS is not yet enabled on the device, use http://IP-ADDRESS only for this local setup. 2. If the browser warns about a local certificate, continue only after confirming that the IP matches the printed status sheet. 3. Sign in with the administrator credentials printed on the product label or supplied in the printer documentation. Change the default password. 4. Reserve the address in the router, or ask the network administrator to configure a suitable static address. The IP address is only for on-site administration. It is not entered in Foody because Server Direct Print uses an outbound connection from the printer to the cloud. 5. Register the printer in FoodyAdmin Open FoodyAdmin → Settings → Printers , then select Register printer . Field Recommended value --- --- Name Physical location: Kitchen , Pizza pass , Bar 1 , or Bar 2 Vendor Epson Server Direct Print Model Exact reference, for example TM-U220IIB-i Epson gateway Direct if this printer polls Foody; otherwise select the registered Epson gateway WebConfig ID A unique ID such as restaurant-kitchen-01 Printer device ID local printer in direct mode; the exact WebConfig device ID in gateway mode Width TM-U220 · 76 mm · 384 dots Interval 2 s Station Select an existing station or create one named after its physical location Select Register . Foody then displays these values once: - Server Direct Print URL; - status notification URL; - WebConfig ID; - password; - Digest realm. Keep this screen open for the next step. The password is not shown again after closing. Do not send it through an unsecured message or photograph. 6. Configure Server Direct Print in WebConfig In TMNet WebConfig, open Server Direct Print and enable it. Copy the values generated by Foody exactly: 1. Server Direct Print URL : the print URL shown by Foody. 2. ID / User ID : the WebConfig ID selected in FoodyAdmin. 3. Password : the one-time password. 4. Device ID : local printer for the built-in printer, or the exact device ID registered behind a gateway. 5. Interval : 2 seconds. Enable Status Notification and enter its Foody URL with the same credentials. Save and apply the configuration, then allow the printer to restart if requested. Do not add spaces before or after the ID, password, or URLs. Foody URLs must remain https:// . 7. Wait for Online and print a test 1. Return to Settings → Printers . 2. Wait up to 15 seconds. Status should move from Unknown to Online , and Last seen should update. 3. Select Test or Print test ticket . 4. Wait for the complete ticket. Foody marks it printed only after the Epson confirms the result. 5. Check the station name, French and Hebrew characters, paper feed, and legibility. If status remains Unknown , the printer is not reaching Foody. If it is Online but the test fails, open Jobs to see the latest device error. 8. Create production stations A station is a logical destination. Menu components route to the station, and the station owns its printer. A failed printer can therefore be replaced without changing the menu. For a four-printer kitchen, a practical layout is: Station Primary printer Typical content --- --- --- Kitchen Kitchen Epson Hot dishes, starters, fried items Pizza pass Pizza Epson Pizzas and pizza extras Bar 1 First bar Epson Drinks and cocktails Bar 2 Second bar Epson A second drinks copy when both bars produce Use Full order copy for an expediter who needs the whole order. A fallback printer does not create a second copy; it is used only when the primary printer is unavailable. To print on both bar printers, create two stations and route drinks to both columns. 9. Route categories and exceptions Open Routing : 1. Check every station that should receive each category. 2. For example, route Pizzas to Pizza pass and Drinks to Bar 1 and Bar 2 . 3. Save the matrix. 4. Add an item override only when an item must leave its category route. 5. Add a modifier override for an independently produced component, such as a sauce sent to the kitchen while the main item goes to the grill. Before enabling server printing, the setup panel should show every printer tested, every station assigned, and every category routed. 10. Send a real Foody ticket 1. Enable Print kitchen tickets from the server . 2. In FoodyPOS, create a test order containing an item from each routed category and a modifier with a special route. 3. Confirm or send the order to the kitchen according to the restaurant workflow. 4. Confirm that each station receives only its lines and that a full-order station receives the complete order. 5. In FoodyAdmin, open Jobs . Each ticket should move from Queued to Awaiting confirmation , then Printed . Do not start live service until this end-to-end test passes. Keep the previous printing method available during the first live order as a temporary precaution. Quick troubleshooting Symptom What to check --- --- No network light Ethernet cable, switch port, and power Address 169.254.x.x The router's DHCP server did not answer WebConfig cannot be reached Same network, correct IP, and guest isolation disabled Server Direct Print is missing Non-intelligent model or incompatible firmware/interface Unknown in Foody Service disabled, wrong URL/ID/password, or blocked DNS/Internet Online but no order ticket Station not assigned, category not routed, or server printing disabled Failed job Open Jobs , fix the paper/cover/ribbon error, then run another test Wrong station Review the category matrix and item/modifier overrides Manufacturer documentation - Epson TM-U220IIB Series - Epson Server Direct Print manual - Lightspeed TM-U220B / TM-U220IIB setup guide WebConfig menu names can vary slightly by firmware and network interface. Do not factory-reset a printer during service. Photograph the product label, network status sheet, and relevant screen before contacting Foody.

articles.title: Printer profiles and routing
articles.description: Open POS → More → Settings → Hardware → Printers/Profiles, or Admin → Settings → Printers.
articles.body: Open POS → More → Settings → Hardware → Printers/Profiles, or Admin → Settings → Printers. Find an Epson printer on the local network 1. Connect the iPad or Victa and the supported Epson printer to the same local network. Switch on the printer and check its paper and cover. Your account must have access to printer settings. 2. Open POS → More → Settings → Hardware → Printers and select Scan network . Opening the page can also start a scan. Wait until the scan finishes. 3. On iPad, allow Local Network access when iOS asks. If the first scan is empty after granting permission, run Scan network again. If access was denied, enable it for FoodyPOS in iPad Settings, then retry. 4. Check the discovered model and IP address. Users with printer-management permission can register discovered printers and assign their profiles; read-only printer access does not register devices. 5. If Scan network is disabled with a notice, the installed build does not enable automatic discovery. Existing configured printers still work. Use Connect a printer → Select a printer → Advanced printer configuration → Epson printer to enter its IP address, or install the supported update when distributed. If no printer is found, check that the Wi-Fi allows local device communication and that the devices are not on isolated guest networks. Manual IP entry remains available when broadcast discovery is blocked. Discovery does not prove printing: deliberately run one test and check the paper before requesting another copy. Create or edit a shared profile Managers can create/edit, disable/reactivate or delete shared profiles. New profiles begin with supported job types off: enable receipt, onsite or online tickets deliberately. A shared edit affects assigned devices; deletion removes routing metadata, not physical printers or job history. Set ticket options Configure categories, one item per ticket, kitchen names, combining identical items, footer, margins, new-category behavior, copies, recipient details, font size and sorting where offered. Common settings are shared within one profile. Save explicitly; failed saves retain your draft. Assign the right printer In Admin assign installation/printer mappings to the intended active profiles. Disabling a profile suspends routing while preserving the assignment. Editing a profile does not replace device mappings. Verify the actual transport and printer identity before a deliberate development test ticket.

articles.title: Printer status and history
articles.description: Open the configured printer’s detail, then Pending document printing → View history.
articles.body: Open the configured printer’s detail, then Pending document printing → View history. Check connectivity Check explicit online/offline/unknown status, power, paper and network. Unknown is not Ready. Star CloudPRNT, compatible Epson/gateway and native Victa paths depend on the actual configured model/transport; USB, Bluetooth or AirPrint are not universally supported. Read the last 24 hours View the paginated last-24-hour history and inspect job kind/state/times. It is read-only and excludes ticket/customer content. Refresh does not claim or reprint jobs. For uncertain printing, reconcile the queued job before requesting another ticket to avoid duplicates.

articles.title: Devices and kitchen displays
articles.description: Open Settings → Devices or Kitchen displays. Configure routing and permissions before using a device in service.
articles.body: Open Settings → Devices or Kitchen displays. Configure routing and permissions before using a device in service. Configure devices Find the correct device, review its identity, active state and selected POS profile. Do not reuse an activation code across restaurants. A staff role and a device profile have different responsibilities; check both if a screen or action is unavailable. Set kitchen stations Create or edit the station and assign its allowed item categories and device access. Review priority and completion behavior. An item can route to its configured production station while keeping its customer-facing menu group unchanged. Work with kitchen tickets Open the assigned KDS, inspect released tickets and advance or complete them using permitted controls. Held food is not a released ticket. Recall/priority actions must target the displayed ticket; do not re-send an order merely because its station is offline.

articles.title: Ordering and fulfillment rules
articles.description: Open Settings → Orders and Fulfillment. These rules affect customer eligibility, beyond the visual Website editor.
articles.body: Open Settings → Orders and Fulfillment. These rules affect customer eligibility, beyond the visual Website editor. Choose ordering channels Review enabled pickup, delivery and table modes and their minimums, fees and preparation settings. Change one rule at a time and inspect its customer-facing explanation. Public ordering can be paused independently of restaurant opening hours. Set scheduling limits Review immediate versus scheduled ordering, lead time, booking horizon and time-slot settings. Batch preorder cutoffs and delivery-tour dates have separate configuration. Verify that an offered slot satisfies all applicable rules. Use temporary test access carefully Temporary test access requires a specific public IP and expiry within seven days. Activation pauses public ordering. Tests create real orders and notifications; use development for test data. Expiry or revocation leaves ordering paused: resume explicitly when ready. Never publish an allowed IP list in a guide or message.

articles.title: Configure the customer ordering assistant
articles.description: Open Settings → AI assistant. This is the restaurant’s customer ordering assistant, separate from the Foody help assistant.
articles.body: Open Settings → AI assistant. This is the restaurant’s customer ordering assistant, separate from the Foody help assistant. Enable and choose a trigger Review enablement, trigger and delay. Choose whether upselling and automatic cart proposals are allowed, then save and verify the saved state. These options do not bypass catalog availability, required choices, ordering rules or payment verification. Maintain guidance and FAQ Write factual guidance, aliases, pairings and FAQ using current restaurant information. Avoid secrets and personal customer data. Test ambiguous requests in each supported language. Use reset/discard to abandon unsaved edits; a failed save does not confirm the new configuration.

articles.title: Notifications and team preferences
articles.description: Open Settings → Notifications or Team, and distinguish personal preferences from restaurant-wide rules.
articles.body: Open Settings → Notifications or Team, and distinguish personal preferences from restaurant-wide rules. Choose notification preferences Select the events and channels offered for the current user/device. Grant browser or OS permission only when prompted for the intended device. Verify permission, subscription and recipient selection if alerts stop; device sound settings may also suppress them. Review team settings Review team defaults in Settings, then manage actual employees, roles and table assignments in Staff. Saving a notification preference does not grant a business permission. Use the staff member’s own account instead of sharing owner credentials.

articles.title: POS behavior, courses and adjustments
articles.description: Open Settings → POS, then the appropriate mode/profile. Legacy Full service settings redirect to the default profile.
articles.body: Open Settings → POS, then the appropriate mode/profile. Legacy Full service settings redirect to the default profile. Set menu behavior Open Menu behavior and choose the options offered for item selection, modifiers and navigation. Assign the intended profile to the POS device. Test with an item that has a required choice so staff cannot accidentally skip it. Configure service courses Open Services and maintain the course names and order used at the restaurant. Review holding/firing behavior in the active POS profile. Courses organize kitchen release; they are distinct from payment splits and customer-facing menu groups. Review allowed adjustments Open Adjustments and review the available reasons and behavior for reductions, offerings and cancellation. Staff still need the corresponding permissions. Library POS discounts and online promotion codes are maintained in their own modules.

articles.title: POS navigation, appearance and shortcuts
articles.description: Open More/Plus on the POS. Destinations are filtered by role and device capabilities.
articles.body: Open More/Plus on the POS. Destinations are filtered by role and device capabilities. Find operational workspaces Use Home shortcuts or More for Analytics, Kitchen, Staff and Settings. Orders contains live, scheduled calendar, production matrix and history views. A missing destination can reflect permission or activation, so check the account/profile instead of reinstalling immediately. Customize the device In Settings choose Appearance and Shortcuts to adjust supported theme/layout and home actions. Hardware and Checkout have separate panels. Review the installed version in account/settings when reporting a problem; do not share a PIN or activation code. Handle connectivity problems Check Internet, the selected restaurant/device and explicit connection status. Refresh before repeating a save, kitchen send or payment. A cloud POS does not guarantee offline ordering, payment or printing; an unknown state must be reconciled before another action.

articles.title: Restaurant profile, languages and hours
articles.description: Open Settings for the selected restaurant. Confirm its name before saving changes.
articles.body: Open Settings for the selected restaurant. Confirm its name before saving changes. Edit restaurant information In general settings update the displayed name, description, contact information and address fields available to your role. In Branding update logo and brand assets. Save and verify the guest-facing result; Website may have its own published design overrides. Set supported languages In Languages choose the restaurant languages and default language offered by the form. Translate catalog names and public website content separately. Changing the interface language alone does not translate every item or customer message. Maintain opening hours In Opening hours edit each day and its time ranges, including closed days. Check the restaurant time zone, calendar exceptions and separate pickup/delivery schedules. Save, then verify the next offered fulfillment slot without placing a real order.

articles.title: Service modes and device profiles
articles.description: Choose between Table Mode (floor plan with table assignments) and Counter Mode (no tables, pickup-style service).
articles.body: Admin → Settings → Devices → Modes Choose a mode profile Review the available mode profiles and select the one intended for the POS device. Check enabled modules and the device assignment before use. Configure table and counter behavior Review seating, covers, service courses, kitchen sending and return-to-menu behavior in the corresponding POS settings. Save and verify on the intended device. Keep fulfillment independent Pickup/delivery choices and prompts are configured separately from the table layout. Check item-level dining options and order-level fulfillment without assuming one replaces the other.

articles.title: Order processing and kitchen workflow
articles.description: Configure auto-kitchen, order approval, rush mode, tips, scheduled orders, and pickup prep time.
articles.body: Admin → Settings → Restaurant → Processing / Workflow Review order acceptance Choose the restaurant’s acceptance policy and review which orders require staff approval. Paid and accepted are distinct statuses; unpaid online orders requiring payment are not sent as paid POS orders. Configure kitchen progression Review automatic/manual kitchen sending and preparation progression. Test one intended order in the agreed test environment and verify its kitchen ticket. Set preparation timing Set the preparation delay/start policy and splitting behavior in the offered controls. Check minute-level values and timezone; guest scheduling is validated by the API. Verify saved settings Save changes, reopen the settings and verify the POS behavior. Resolve a save error before expecting other devices to use the draft.

articles.title: POS access, devices and shifts
articles.description: Admin → Staff → POS access / Shift reports
articles.body: Admin → Staff → POS access / Shift reports Activate a POS device Review the restaurant device list and follow the device setup pairing flow. Confirm the device belongs to the intended restaurant before authorizing access. Use a personal POS code After activation, use the configured employee POS code. End your service or switch employee using the POS controls instead of sharing a manager session. Review shift reports Choose the report period and employee/device filters, then inspect recorded start/end times. A missing end time must be investigated rather than assumed closed.

articles.title: Employees and invitations
articles.description: Add employees, review invitation delivery and assign restaurant roles.
articles.body: Admin → Staff → Employees Availability and access Requires staff management permission for invitations and changes. Invite an employee Enter the name, email, optional phone and restaurant role, then submit. Read the invitation delivery result separately from employee creation. Resend an invitation Open the employee profile and use its invitation action after correcting an address or delivery problem. Check the new result. Review and remove access Review role, account status and POS code configuration. Use removal only for the intended employee; owner controls remain protected.

articles.title: Roles and permissions
articles.description: Admin → Staff → Roles and permissions
articles.body: Admin → Staff → Roles and permissions Availability and access Requires role-management permission; restaurant scope always applies. Create a role Open the role library, create a named role and select the required permissions. Save before assigning employees. Assign and verify Assign the role from the employee profile. Verify the permitted pages and actions with that employee; menu visibility alone is not proof of authorization. Change or retire a role Review assigned employees before changing permissions or deleting a role. Respect protected system/owner roles and check resulting access after saving.

articles.title: Floor plans, tables and QR codes
articles.description: Create your dining room layout in FoodyAdmin and use it to manage tables in FoodyPOS.
articles.body: Admin → Settings → Restaurant → Floor plans / Table QR Create a floor plan Create a named floor plan, add the required tables and arrange their position, shape and capacity using the editor. Save before opening it on the POS. Organize service sections Review restaurant sections and table assignments. Keep table identities stable when rearranging a plan; moving a drawing is different from moving a financial check. Prepare table QR cards Open table QR settings, select the intended table and customize the available card style/text. Download or print the offered output and scan it to verify restaurant and table. Use the live table view Select the correct floor plan on the POS and inspect table status before opening a check. Review covers/seats separately and confirm the saved check before payment or transfer.

articles.title: Create and print table QR cards
articles.description: Open Restaurant → Table QR, then Customize or Print.
articles.body: Open Restaurant → Table QR, then Customize or Print. Customize the QR card Select a card layout, text, logo/image and colors, then adjust the available typography roles: font, weight, case, size, letter spacing and color. Check Hebrew glyph support and contrast. QR readability takes priority over decoration. Print and verify table destinations Choose the intended tables and print/export options. Scan a sample from the actual printed size and verify restaurant/table before placing it in service. Replaced or expired signed links require refreshed cards; do not manually edit encoded IDs/signatures.

articles.title: Table access, status and assistance
articles.description: Open Staff → Table service to assign access. Table status and assistance are configured under Settings.
articles.body: Open Staff → Table service to assign access. Table status and assistance are configured under Settings. Assign rooms, sections and tables Choose free, collaborative or strict assignment mode, read its displayed access rule, then modify an eligible staff member’s assignment. Select rooms, sections or specific tables and review the resulting covered-table count. Staff with unrestricted table access remain explicitly identified. Maintain table state Review the available status labels and table/session controls. An occupied table can have multiple bills: check the active session and covers before seating, moving or closing. Changing a visual status is not proof that a bill was paid. Configure assistance requests In Table assistance enable the supported requests and staff notifications appropriate to service. Check the assigned staff/device recipients. On the service screen acknowledge or resolve the request after attending the guest; an assistance request does not create a payment.

articles.title: Catering and chain entry pages
articles.description: Select the catering or chain order-entry page in Website. The service catalog and branch activation are managed separately.
articles.body: Select the catering or chain order-entry page in Website. The service catalog and branch activation are managed separately. Customize catering presentation Edit the page heading, introduction, service subtitles and available layout options. An empty override inherits the original service text; use reset to restore inheritance. Only active services can be presented. Confirm the service’s separate availability and quote settings. Customize branch selection Edit branch-selector copy in French, Hebrew and English and the available appearance options. Check that the chain page links to the intended active branch and ordering mode. Publishing a design does not grant a branch new permissions, a menu or payment credentials.

articles.title: Checkout, confirmation and digital receipt design
articles.description: In Website open the order journey screens. Their appearance is separate from payment-provider configuration.
articles.body: In Website open the order journey screens. Their appearance is separate from payment-provider configuration. Preview checkout and confirmation Select checkout then confirmation, adjust available colors and text, and inspect mobile readability. Required customer, fulfillment and payment fields come from restaurant policy. A preview does not place an order or verify a live payment connection. Set receipt content and actions On the receipt screen set localized title/message and compact or comfortable layout. Toggle logo, address, phone, status and customer information, then print, share, order history and new-order actions. Preview each language; publish to make the settings public. These controls do not alter the recorded transaction or fiscal document.

articles.title: Edit and publish your restaurant website
articles.description: Understand the difference between a saved draft, preview and a published site.
articles.body: Open the corresponding Foody workspace described below. Open the website editor In FoodyAdmin, open your restaurant’s Website workspace. Choose a page or section and edit its content, images or appearance. The preview shows the current draft. Saving is different from publishing Changes are saved as a draft. An autosaved draft does not replace the site your customers see. 1. Edit the required page or section. 2. Wait for the draft to finish saving and check the preview. 3. Use Publish to make the reviewed draft public. 4. Wait for a successful result, then verify the public link on the intended device. If publishing fails, the preview alone does not prove the public site changed. Keep your draft and resolve the reported error. Discard restores the published state and removes unpublished edits; use it only when you intend to abandon the draft. Menu and ordering content Website appearance does not replace menu configuration. Items must belong to a menu group with the right channel and hours. Check the ordering page and the relevant pickup, delivery or table context after publishing. Menus and groups

articles.title: Website design and branding
articles.description: Open Website, then Site design. Work in the draft and preview both desktop and mobile before publishing.
articles.body: Open Website, then Site design. Work in the draft and preview both desktop and mobile before publishing. Choose a theme and colors Select the theme, brand color and color style. Use custom background, text, muted, accent and divider colors where offered. Check text contrast on every background. A section override affects that section; site settings provide inherited defaults. Set fonts and text roles Choose the font pairing or heading/body fonts. For ordering, adjust category title, item name, description and price roles separately. Check Hebrew direction and long names; a desktop size may need a separate mobile setting. Frame item images Choose fit, crop and focal point in the image controls. Compare the card and item detail preview on both screen sizes. Keep text outside image assets when it needs translation. Save the draft, then publish only after checking the public page.

articles.title: Header, navigation and footer
articles.description: Select the header or footer in the Website editor. These site-wide regions are distinct from a page section.
articles.body: Select the header or footer in the Website editor. These site-wide regions are distinct from a page section. Configure the header Choose logo, name visibility, logo size/position and link alignment. Compare transparent/overlay and scrolled/solid states, including their separate text colors and optional scrolled logo. Preview the mobile hamburger menu. Manage links and the main button Add or edit a navigation link, choose its destination and order. Enable the main button if needed; set its label, link, shape, size and appearance in both header states. Open each destination in preview. A link alone does not publish an unpublished page. Configure footer content Choose layout and visibility, then select logo, description, address, phone, opening hours and social links to display. Edit custom text and the Foody branding options separately. Use valid public social/contact links and check them after publishing.

articles.title: Design the online ordering page
articles.description: In Website choose the order page and switch between page and item-detail surfaces. Catalog data remains managed in Menu.
articles.body: In Website choose the order page and switch between page and item-detail surfaces. Catalog data remains managed in Menu. Choose menu layout and navigation Select the displayed menu and desktop/mobile layout. Configure group banners, category navigation, prices and descriptions with the available controls. Menu groups control public ordering structure; internal categories do not create public sections. Customize item details Select the item-detail preview to edit cover image and display options. Test a real configured item with variants, required modifiers, quantities and notes. Design changes do not change its base price, modifier deltas, stock or ordering eligibility. Place discovery content Edit discovery heading, image position, card height/radius and panel colors. Choose its placement relative to the menu/group or after a number of items where supported. Preview empty and populated groups on mobile before publication.

articles.title: Website pages, SEO and publication
articles.description: Open Website and the page list. Page settings are staged in the draft before public publication.
articles.body: Open Website and the page list. Page settings are staged in the draft before public publication. Add a page Choose Add page, preview a library template or select an available page type, name it and choose whether to add it to navigation. Review the public address and menu/service association for commerce pages. Reserved or duplicate addresses are rejected. Confirm creation to add it to the draft. Edit page identity and navigation Open Page settings → General. Change name, editable address, navigation inclusion and menu association where offered. Some special commerce addresses cannot be edited. Check links to a changed address and do not assume old external links redirect automatically. Set search and sharing metadata In SEO set title and description and inspect the search preview. In Social choose or remove the sharing image and review the preview. Save the staged settings and verify each public language after publication. Search engines and messaging caches control when their previews refresh. Publish and verify the draft Preview desktop/mobile, public navigation, commerce availability and links, then Publish deliberately. Reopen the public page to verify the result. Unsaved/staged changes are not evidence of public publication. Review page references before a confirmed deletion and use discard/reset only for changes you intend to abandon.

articles.title: Page sections, media and animation
articles.description: Open a content or landing page, select a section in the canvas or sidebar, and use its content, appearance and animation panels.
articles.body: Open a content or landing page, select a section in the canvas or sidebar, and use its content, appearance and animation panels. Add, move and hide sections Add an available section type, edit it, and reorder it on the page. Visibility hides the section without deleting its content. Moving a section to another page changes its location. Review the draft before confirming deletion. Write and select content Edit headings, subtitle, body and button links for text/image, hero, feature cards and supporting content. Choose the items or menu groups for menu highlights and featured items. Contact sections can show address, phone, hours and social links. Check each language rather than embedding untranslated text in pictures. Set images and video Upload or select media, adjust fit, overlay, background, width, height and spacing where available. For video choose controls, autoplay, loop and muted state. Browsers can restrict autoplay; check the actual mobile page and retain readable text while media loads. Preview animation Enable motion only where useful. Set entrance, duration, delay, replay, hover and parallax; mobile motion can have separate settings. For rotating text/carousels set phrases, interval and transition speed. Test reduced-motion behavior and avoid motion that hides essential information.

articles.title: Sécurité du compte et clés d’accès
articles.description: Admin → Paramètres → Sécurité
articles.body: Admin → Paramètres → Sécurité Ajouter une clé d’accès Ouvrez la sécurité dans un navigateur compatible et enregistrez une clé d’accès avec la confirmation de l’appareil. Vérifiez sa présence dans la liste du compte. Se connecter avec une clé d’accès Choisissez la connexion par clé d’accès et terminez la vérification du navigateur ou de l’appareil. Le déverrouillage ne donne pas de permissions supplémentaires sur le restaurant. Retirer une clé inutilisée Sélectionnez une clé inutilisée dans la sécurité et confirmez sa suppression. Conservez une méthode de connexion utilisable avant de retirer la dernière clé. En cas d’échec Si la vérification de l’appareil échoue, conservez la clé existante et utilisez une autre méthode configurée.

articles.title: Abonnement et facturation
articles.description: Admin → Compte → Facturation, si proposé
articles.body: Admin → Compte → Facturation, si proposé Lire l’abonnement actuel Vérifiez formule enregistrée, statut et date d’essai, renouvellement ou grâce pertinente. Confirmez les conditions commerciales avec Foody ; les libellés techniques peuvent différer des offres actuelles. Vérifier un changement de formule Le propriétaire autorisé vérifie puis confirme le changement proposé. Attendez la relecture de l’abonnement ; en cas d’incertitude, vérifiez la formule avant une nouvelle demande. Consulter les événements de facturation Consultez type, date, montant et devise des événements. Contactez le support pour un échec inexpliqué ou abonnement bloqué ; les paiements de commandes sont distincts de l’abonnement logiciel.

articles.title: Assistant métier du restaurant
articles.description: Ouvrez le panneau IA métier Admin avec un compte autorisé. Ce panneau est distinct de l’assistant d’aide public.
articles.body: Ouvrez le panneau IA métier Admin avec un compte autorisé. Ce panneau est distinct de l’assistant d’aide public. Interroger les données métier Choisissez le restaurant et posez une question précise sur ventes, meilleurs articles, stock, commandes, clients, personnel ou menu. Vérifiez la réponse dans l’écran source. L’interprétation IA ne prouve pas un rapprochement de paiement et ne remplace pas la comptabilité. Comprendre le périmètre du panneau Les requêtes métier utilisent le restaurant connecté. L’assistant public ne reçoit que guides et conversation. N’y collez pas exports métier/client, mots de passe ni cartes. Pour une réponse non étayée, utilisez le module source ou le responsable autorisé.

articles.title: Lire le tableau de bord et les rapports
articles.description: Choisir la base de date et comprendre les commandes comptabilisées.
articles.body: Ouvrez l’espace Foody correspondant décrit ci-dessous. Commencer par l’accueil Ouvrez Accueil dans FoodyAdmin. Le tableau de bord présente la période ou le service choisi, les commandes à traiter, les ventes brutes, le nombre de commandes, le ticket moyen, les articles vendus et les commandes récentes. Les accès dépendent de vos permissions. Vérifier la base de date Le sélecteur peut utiliser la date des commandes ou un service/série planifié. Un service à venir peut déjà afficher des commandes reçues pour ce service : ces chiffres ne signifient pas qu’il est terminé. Vérifiez la base de date avant de comparer avec un autre rapport. Le contrôle Commandes comptabilisées précise le calcul, par exemple les commandes payées ou acceptées. Des ventes sur commandes acceptées ne prouvent pas que tous les paiements sont encaissés. Consultez séparément les paiements demandant votre attention. Comparaisons et données indisponibles Les comparaisons nécessitent une période ou un service précédent disponible. Pour un service à venir ou en cours, le tableau de bord explique l’absence de comparaison. Une donnée indisponible est différente d’une période vide : actualisez ou résolvez l’erreur de chargement avant d’interpréter une valeur absente comme zéro. Rapports détaillés Ouvrez Rapports pour accéder aux pages autorisées par votre rôle. Choisissez la période et vérifiez les filtres. La vue d’ensemble propose une action d’export ; contrôlez que la période et le calcul exportés correspondent à votre analyse.

articles.title: Établissements et routage catering
articles.description: Ouvrez Catering → Établissements et Routage.
articles.body: Ouvrez Catering → Établissements et Routage. Maintenir les établissements éligibles Créez/modifiez informations et activation de l’établissement. Vérifiez rattachement au restaurant et associations de services. Un établissement inactif ne doit pas servir de nouvelle destination client. Régler les règles de routage Créez/modifiez une règle avec service, destination et conditions proposées. Vérifiez priorité/ordre et conflits. Contrôlez une demande représentative et confirmez avant suppression d’une règle utilisée.

articles.title: Événements catering et solde
articles.description: Ouvrez Catering → Événements et l’événement concerné.
articles.body: Ouvrez Catering → Événements et l’événement concerné. Vérifier l’événement accepté Vérifiez date/heure, établissement, convives, configuration, statut et paiements. Utilisez les actions après contrôle des besoins de production et affectations. Approbation du devis, avancement et paiement sont distincts. Gérer une autorisation de solde compatible Ouvrez le panneau solde et lisez l’état. Créez/partagez un lien ou encaissez seulement si l’action est autorisée par prestataire et état de l’événement. Réconciliez une autorisation ambiguë avant nouvelle opération. Une autorisation n’est pas un encaissement.

articles.title: Questions, planning et tarifs catering
articles.description: Dans l’éditeur du service, ouvrez parcours client et tarifs. Utilisez le simulateur avant publication.
articles.body: Dans l’éditeur du service, ouvrez parcours client et tarifs. Utilisez le simulateur avant publication. Configurer les étapes client Maintenez ordre, questions obligatoires et choix uniques. Réglez planning, convives, événement et sélections disponibles. Vérifiez libellés traduits et chaque branche ; changer une question peut modifier les conditions tarifaires. Maintenir les règles tarifaires Choisissez article, tarif de base/repli et conditions : convives, jour, créneau ou réponse. Évitez les règles spécifiques qui se chevauchent. Dans le simulateur, choisissez un contexte représentatif et vérifiez tarif résolu et avertissements avant enregistrement.

articles.title: Examiner les devis catering
articles.description: Ouvrez Catering → Devis et sélectionnez la demande. Vérifiez statut et configuration complète.
articles.body: Ouvrez Catering → Devis et sélectionnez la demande. Vérifiez statut et configuration complète. Approuver ou refuser un devis Vérifiez demande, date, convives, sélections, total et acompte. Si autorisé, ajustez le total et ajoutez une note, puis approuvez ou refusez. Vérifiez le statut enregistré ; une demande en attente n’est pas un événement accepté. Vérifier acompte et preuve de remboursement Distinguez acompte principal et doublon enregistré. Si Rembourser est disponible, choisissez cible et montant puis confirmez une fois. Pour un remboursement externe, effectuez-le d’abord chez le prestataire puis enregistrez sa référence obligatoire dans Foody. Cet enregistrement ne transfère pas l’argent. Un résultat incertain exige vérification avant nouvelle tentative.

articles.title: Services, catalogue et offres catering
articles.description: Ouvrez Catering → Services, puis un service et ses panneaux catalogue/offres.
articles.body: Ouvrez Catering → Services, puis un service et ses panneaux catalogue/offres. Créer et activer un service Créez nom, description, adresse et langues, puis vérifiez état actif, mode de devis et acompte. Enregistrez avant d’ajouter sa page publique. Un service actif nécessite encore configuration publique et disponibilité adaptées. Maintenir groupes et articles Ajoutez groupes et articles du service, modifiez descriptions, images/galerie, activation et prix. Vérifiez choix autorisés et quantités par portion/convive. Ce catalogue est distinct des groupes POS ; vérifiez le service avant modification. Composer offres et formules Créez/modifiez l’offre, ses articles inclus et contraintes de choix. Prévisualisez parcours client et total. Publiez après vérification de tous les articles, quantités et choix obligatoires.

articles.title: Chaînes et gestion des établissements
articles.description: Ouvrez Chaîne/Établissements ou le tableau de bord de chaîne avec un compte autorisé.
articles.body: Ouvrez Chaîne/Établissements ou le tableau de bord de chaîne avec un compte autorisé. Choisir le bon établissement Sélectionnez chaîne et établissement, puis vérifiez le contexte avant modification de menu, stock, personnel ou paiement. Une présentation de chaîne partagée ne rend pas les données des restaurants interchangeables. Vérifier la présence publique Maintenez informations et présence site/commande, puis vérifiez sélecteur et destination. Contrôlez séparément menus actifs, horaires, remise et paiement de chaque restaurant avant publication.

articles.title: Modèles et automatisations de messages
articles.description: Ouvrez Paramètres → Modèles de messages, modèles WhatsApp ou Workflow selon le canal.
articles.body: Ouvrez Paramètres → Modèles de messages, modèles WhatsApp ou Workflow selon le canal. Créer et vérifier un modèle Modifiez textes localisés et variables, ou soumettez un modèle WhatsApp Utility via le prestataire. Vérifiez approbation, langue et ordre des variables. La suppression peut être bloquée même si l’étape qui le référence est désactivée. Associer les messages aux étapes Choisissez un modèle approuvé sur l’étape et son déclenchement. Les messages concernent les futures entrées, sans reprise historique. Rappels livraison exigent données livreur/date ; satisfaction exige remise enregistrée. Lisez le déclencheur, sans supposer un envoi systématique la veille.

articles.title: Connecter et utiliser WhatsApp
articles.description: Ouvrez Paramètres → WhatsApp. Choisissez le mode de connexion/facturation compatible avant les identifiants.
articles.body: Ouvrez Paramètres → WhatsApp. Choisissez le mode de connexion/facturation compatible avant les identifiants. Connecter un expéditeur Utilisez la connexion Foody ou le compte Twilio propre au restaurant si proposé. L’expéditeur personnel doit déjà être enregistré/en ligne avec modèles Utility approuvés du même compte. Entrez les secrets uniquement dans le formulaire. Un échec conserve la configuration ; changez de facturation après déconnexion. Utiliser Meta coexistence sous activation Meta coexistence direct est un pilote contrôlé, désactivé par défaut. Connecter ne change pas le routage ; activez explicitement le prestataire voulu après vérification. L’application Business est conservée. N’attendez pas un repli Twilio automatique en cas d’échec Meta. Lire l’historique des messages Dans la communication de commande, consultez envoyé, livré, lu, échec et blocage avant envoi. Un blocage ne prouve pas une livraison. Le rappel livreur relu se déclenche par son action éligible. Un résultat prestataire inconnu n’est pas rejoué automatiquement ; vérifiez avant renvoi.

articles.title: Clients, adresses et doublons
articles.description: Admin → Clients
articles.body: Admin → Clients Disponibilité et accès La modification et la fusion nécessitent la permission de gestion des clients. Retrouver un client Recherchez dans la liste et vérifiez nom, téléphone, adresse, nombre de commandes et dernière commande. Confirmez la bonne personne avant modification. Modifier les coordonnées de livraison Ouvrez la fiche, corrigez téléphone, adresse et précisions de livraison, puis enregistrez. Vérifiez séparément l’adresse des commandes déjà créées. Autoriser la commande en espèces Utilisez le réglage client de confiance/espèces uniquement pour le client concerné. Il autorise la commande en espèces et ne prouve aucun encaissement. Fusionner des doublons Vérifiez les fiches sélectionnées et numéros avant de confirmer une fusion. Contrôlez la fiche résultante et ne fusionnez pas des personnes différentes.

articles.title: Parcours coursier et confirmation des livraisons
articles.description: Admin → Commandes → Mode coursier, ou espace coursier affecté
articles.body: Admin → Commandes → Mode coursier, ou espace coursier affecté Ouvrir la tournée affectée Ouvrez la tournée affectée et vérifiez date, ordre des arrêts et créneaux. Utilisez uniquement les commandes de votre périmètre coursier autorisé. Naviguer et contacter Ouvrez l’application de navigation proposée et consultez contact et consignes. Validez une adresse corrigée avec le dispatch avant de changer le plan. Confirmer le résultat réel Utilisez l’action de statut après la remise réelle. Renseignez les informations demandées et vérifiez l’enregistrement ; une livraison confirmée n’encaisse pas seule un solde impayé.

articles.title: Dispatch et planification des tournées
articles.description: Admin → Commandes → Livraisons / Tournées
articles.body: Admin → Commandes → Livraisons / Tournées Choisir les livraisons d’une date Choisissez la date de tournée et vérifiez les commandes disponibles. Ne mélangez pas les livraisons planifiées d’un autre jour de service. Affecter coursiers et arrêts Choisissez coursier, dépôt et commandes, puis vérifiez adresses, temps de remise et créneaux promis. Corrigez les adresses avant optimisation. Vérifier une tournée calculée Lancez le calcul ou l’affectation de flotte proposés puis vérifiez avant enregistrement/dispatch. Distinguez conduite, attente et remise ; les recalculs peuvent consommer des usages fournisseur. Enregistrer et suivre l’avancement Enregistrez la tournée vérifiée puis utilisez le dispatch. Suivez coursier et commandes et modifiez explicitement un plan devenu obsolète.

articles.title: Fournisseurs de cartes et usages
articles.description: Admin → Paramètres → Livraison → Cartes
articles.body: Admin → Paramètres → Livraison → Cartes Vérifier le fournisseur configuré Consultez fournisseur actif et usages disponibles. Conservez les identifiants dans la configuration sécurisée prévue ; ne les collez jamais dans le chat. Respecter les limites d’usage Vérifiez limites de cartes, recherche d’adresses et itinéraires/optimisation avant une grande planification. Une offre commerciale n’active pas automatiquement un quota ni ne contourne une limite fournisseur.

articles.title: Zones, frais et calendriers de livraison
articles.description: Admin → Paramètres → Livraison
articles.body: Admin → Paramètres → Livraison Créer une zone de livraison Créez ou modifiez une zone nommée avec les contrôles carte/adresse. Vérifiez périmètre, état actif et éligibilité des commandes avant enregistrement. Définir frais et minimums Réglez frais et minimum de commande de la zone. Testez adresse et panier aux limites ; les frais de livraison sont distincts du coût d’un transporteur externe. Configurer jours et créneaux Réglez calendrier et fenêtres proposés. Si l’horaire final est en attente, conservez cet état puis confirmez le vrai créneau depuis la planification.

articles.title: Configurer votre restaurant avec Foody
articles.description: Vérifier dans l’ordre les accès, menus, appareils et commandes en ligne.
articles.body: Ouvrez l’espace Foody correspondant décrit ci-dessous. Vérifier la configuration avec votre interlocuteur Foody 1. Activez votre compte et sélectionnez le bon restaurant. Connexion. 2. Vérifiez le profil, les horaires et les paramètres de commande et de service adaptés à votre activité. 3. Créez les articles, puis placez-les dans les groupes des cartes clients. Contrôlez canaux, horaires, prix, variantes et modificateurs. Articles et menus. 4. Vérifiez les rôles, invitations employés et appareils POS activés. Accès équipe. 5. Pour la commande en ligne, vérifiez le brouillon du site, publiez-le, puis ouvrez le lien public. Publication du site. 6. Confirmez avec Foody le prestataire de paiement et la configuration des reçus et imprimantes avant les commandes réelles. Paiements. 7. Testez le parcours prévu dans l’environnement de test convenu, préparation et remise comprises. Contrôlez le résultat du paiement séparément du statut de la commande. Les modules, matériels et moyens de paiement activés dépendent de votre installation et de votre contrat. Faites confirmer la configuration par Foody. N’utilisez pas de paiements réels comme transactions de test.

articles.title: Se connecter et récupérer un accès
articles.description: Accéder à l’Admin et à la caisse avec votre compte du restaurant.
articles.body: Connexion Admin et menu du compte Activer une invitation Ouvrez l’invitation reçue, vérifiez le restaurant et terminez l’activation. Demandez au responsable de renvoyer une invitation expirée. Sélectionner le restaurant Connectez-vous avec votre compte puis choisissez un restaurant autorisé. Vérifiez son nom avant toute modification ou export. Récupérer l’accès Suivez la procédure de récupération proposée ou contactez le responsable. Ne partagez jamais de mot de passe, lien d’activation ou code POS avec l’assistant.

articles.title: Comment tout s'articule : de l'ingrédient au plat épuisé
articles.description: La vue d'ensemble — comment le stock, les préparations, les recettes, les articles, la disponibilité, le coût matière et les commandes s'imbriquent, et dans quel ordre les configurer.
articles.body: Ouvrez l’espace Foody correspondant décrit ci-dessous. La vue d'ensemble Six éléments fonctionnent ensemble. Une fois la chaîne comprise, tout devient clair : - Stock — les ingrédients bruts que vous achetez (tomates, thon, huile, pains). - Préparations — ce que vous fabriquez à partir du stock par lots (une sauce, une pâte, une marinade). - Recette — ce qu'un plat utilise : ses ingrédients et préparations, avec les quantités. - Article — un plat de votre menu, montré aux clients dans un groupe de menu. - Disponibilité — calculée depuis la recette + le stock actuel : stock faible ou épuisé, automatiquement. - Coût matière — également calculé depuis la recette. Le flux : Stock ┐ ├─→ Recette ─→ Article ─→ montré aux clients Préparations ┘ │ ├─→ Disponibilité (faible / épuisé, automatique) └─→ Coût matière (marge par plat) Une commande est passée ─→ la recette est déduite du Stock ─→ la disponibilité se met à jour Un plat n'est donc pas isolé : il pointe vers une recette, la recette pointe vers le stock et les préparations, et ce seul lien fait fonctionner la disponibilité et le coût matière tout seuls. Configurez dans cet ordre Configurez dans cet ordre 1. Ajoutez vos ingrédients au Stock Saisissez les ingrédients bruts que vous achetez, avec leur unité et leur quantité actuelle. → Gestion du stock 2. (Optionnel) Créez vos Préparations Si vous faites des sauces, pâtes ou bases par lots, définissez-les une fois et réutilisez-les sur plusieurs plats. Produire un lot crédite le stock ; les plats concernés redeviennent disponibles automatiquement. → Préparations 3. Créez vos articles Ajoutez chaque plat à votre catalogue (nom, prix, photo, catégorie). → Créer un article 4. Donnez une recette à chaque article Dans l'onglet Recette de l'article, liez les ingrédients et préparations qu'une portion utilise, avec les quantités. C'est ce lien qui alimente tout le reste. Un plat sans recette est toujours disponible et n'a pas de coût calculé. → Ingrédients & portions 5. Placez les articles dans un groupe de menu Les articles n'apparaissent aux clients qu'une fois placés dans un groupe de menu. → Catégories & articles 6. La disponibilité fonctionne alors toute seule Une fois les recettes en place, les plats passent en stock faible et épuisé automatiquement à mesure que le stock baisse, et reviennent quand vous réapprovisionnez. Ajustez avec des règles, ou forcez un plat précis. → Disponibilité Ce que vous obtenez une fois la chaîne connectée - Épuisé automatique — fini de désactiver les plats à la main quand un ingrédient manque. - Coût matière exact — la marge par plat, calculée depuis la recette. - Stock auto-actualisé — chaque commande déduit sa recette, vos chiffres restent justes. - Un seul endroit à modifier — changez la recette d'une préparation une fois et tous les plats suivent. Pour aller plus loin - Prendre et gérer les commandes → Gérer les commandes - Être payé → Comment fonctionnent les paiements - Liste de configuration initiale → Guide de configuration complet

articles.title: Offres, démonstration et contact Foody
articles.description: Visitez foody-pos.co.il, choisissez français, hébreu ou anglais, puis Produits, Tarifs, Démonstration ou Contact.
articles.body: Visitez foody-pos.co.il, choisissez français, hébreu ou anglais, puis Produits, Tarifs, Démonstration ou Contact. Comparer les offres publiques Comparez POS, Commandes, Restaurant, Cuisine et offre combinée avec leurs inclusions. Compagnon appartient à Cuisine. Une licence couvre un appareil, pas un supplément par employé. Consultez les tarifs approuvés et le devis pour matériel, paiement externe, SMS et intégrations. Demander une démonstration ou de l’aide Utilisez Démonstration/Contact avec les coordonnées professionnelles demandées et attendez la confirmation. Le centre d’aide public est à /fr/help, /he/help et /en/help. L’assistant explique les procédures publiées sans accès ni modification de compte. N’envoyez ni secrets ni données de carte.

articles.title: Rechercher et naviguer dans FoodyAdmin
articles.description: Utilisez la recherche de navigation Admin pour le restaurant sélectionné.
articles.body: Utilisez la recherche de navigation Admin pour le restaurant sélectionné. Retrouver une fiche métier Ouvrez la recherche, saisissez un terme assez précis et consultez résultats articles, commandes, clients et stock. Flèches et Entrée ouvrent ; Échap ferme.
